slides.0.title: Santorini and the Aegean Islands
slides.0.subtitle: Volcano, wind and old vines
slides.1.title: Santorini PDO
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Dry whites led by Assyrtiko
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Assyrtiko at least 85% (official Wines of Greece PDO page), with Athiri and Aidani making up at most 15% together; many wines are 100% Assyrtiko
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Nykteri
slides.1.highlights.1.content: A dry style; at least 13.5% ABV and at least 3 months in oak
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Vinsanto
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Sun-dried over-ripe grapes (at least 370 g/L sugar), at least 51% Assyrtiko and at least 24 months of oxidative maturation, with an optional age statement (e.g. 4, 8, 12 years or more)
slides.1.highlights.3.title: Old, ungrafted vines
slides.1.highlights.3.content: Many vines are ungrafted, some rootstocks estimated at 300+ years
slides.1.content: Exam focus: Santorini's stylistic spectrum — dry white, Nykteri, Vinsanto — all rests on Assyrtiko.
slides.2.title: Paros and Lemnos
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Paros
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Covers the whole island; dry white is 100% Monemvasia; dry red is at least 35% Mandilaria blended with Monemvasia; old vines are largely ungrafted; there is also a Malvasia Paros PDO
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Lemnos
slides.2.highlights.1.content: White is 100% Muscat of Alexandria (dry to medium-sweet); dry red uses Limnio; there are also sweet reds from sun-dried grapes
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Muscat of Lemnos
slides.2.content: Lemnos's Limnio appeared in Level 1 and was already mentioned by Aristotle.
slides.3.title: Samos and Rhodes
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Samos
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Muscat Blanc à Petits Grains (locally Moschato Aspro) is 98% of plantings; styles include Vin Doux, Vin Doux Naturel, Grand Cru, Anthemis and Nectar; stone terraces from sea level to about 900 m
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Rhodes
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Red is 100% Mandilaria and white 100% Athiri; there is also a Muscat of Rhodes PDO
slides.3.content: What island PDOs share: one or few grapes, strong sun and a sweet-wine tradition (Muscat).
slides.4.title: Common logic of island terroir
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Wind
slides.4.highlights.0.content: Strong wind lowers disease pressure and forces low training such as kouloura
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Drought
slides.4.highlights.1.content: Little rain means mostly dry-farmed, low yields
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Poor soils
slides.4.highlights.2.content: Volcanic ash, pumice and limestone limit vigour and raise concentration
slides.4.highlights.3.title: Tourism pressure
slides.4.highlights.3.content: On Paros, for example, tourism-driven building and workforce change have limited viticulture
slides.4.content: These four points can go straight into a Diploma essay: wind, drought, poor soil, tourism.
slides.5.componentProps.slide.title: 🧠 Knowledge Check
Vinsanto is made from sun-dried grapes and aged for long periods in oxidative oak.
Which grape underpins the Samos PDO?
A. Muscat Blanc à Petits Grains
Samos is a Muscat sweet-wine area.
Which grape is used for PDO Rhodes red?
Rhodes red is 100% Mandilaria and white 100% Athiri.
